w: Louis XIII had this fortress built in 1624-1627 after Montpellier's rebellions, a stone reminder of who was in charge. It later became the Joffre Barracks, named for the WWI marshal, and since 1947 has housed the nationally famous Lycee Joffre -- lessons taught inside a citadel.
s: A royal fortress that's now a famous lycee
_facts: Early Modern fortification built 1624-1627 under orders of Louis XIII after rebellions
became the Joffre Barracks, named after Joseph Joffre, in the 20th century
since 1947 an academic campus, the nationally known Lycee Joffre

w: Walled and triangular on Avenue de Palavas, this is the only Protestant cemetery left standing in Montpellier -- the fourth the city ever had -- and its oldest cemetery still in active use. A quiet corner for a city that spent centuries arguing over religion.
s: Montpellier's oldest cemetery still in use
_facts: historic, church-owned Protestant cemetery, triangular and walled, on Avenue de Palavas
fourth and only surviving Protestant cemetery in Montpellier
the oldest active cemetery in the city

w: Once the Grand Odeon, this 1,000-capacity room has been a monument historique since 2007 -- rare status for a rock venue. Motorhead, Metallica, Hole and Blue Oyster Cult have all played here, proof that heritage protection and a mosh pit aren't mutually exclusive.
s: A monument-historique venue that hosted Metallica
_facts: 1,000-capacity concert hall, formerly known as the Grand Odeon
artists performed here include Motorhead, Metallica, Hole and Blue Oyster Cult

w: Sheathed in pink marble and closing the view down the Esplanade, this Claude Vasconi-designed hall opened in 1988 after years of political rowing over its cost. Inside, the 2,000-seat Opera Berlioz -- named for the composer -- has hosted the city's opera company since 1990.
s: A pink-marble hall that split 1980s Montpellier
_facts: conference centre and opera house designed by Claude Vasconi, opened 1988, clad in pink marble
closes the visual axis of the Esplanade seen from Place de la Comedie
high building costs were a political controversy under mayor Georges Freche; Opera Berlioz seats 2,000 and has hosted Opera National de Montpellier since 1990

w: Built from 1715 to a plan by architect Jean Giral, this is one of the folies -- country houses -- that Montpellier's merchants scattered around the city's edges. The interior hasn't changed since: antique furniture, portraits, and paintings by Jacques-Louis David, plus a garden fountain built from seashells.
_facts: one of the folies (country houses) built by wealthy 18th-century merchants outside Montpellier
grounds bought 1706, built from 1715 to architect Jean Giral's plan, Renaissance-style facade
interior kept intact since the 18th century with paintings including works by Jacques-Louis David; garden includes a fountain built of seashells
